focus: The flowchart rules sk-design-diagram actually enforces
noveltyJustification: All six findings are new rule-level evidence; only the existence of the diagram skill was previously known.
ruledOut: Reusing the HTML/SVG renderer for FigJam

graphEvents.label: Which flow rules carry over to FigJam

label: The flowchart type uses a shape-carries-type grammar: oval for start/end, rectangle for step, diamond for a decision with at most three exits, and a filled dot for a merge point.
Layout rules: top-to-bottom flow, Yes right and No below from a diamond, every outgoing arrow labelled, coral only on the happy path or one consequential decision, arc jump for crossings.
Three anti-patterns are named: fill color signalling node type, a decision with four or more exits, and unlabelled decision branches.
The ASCII validator already machine-checks decision labelling and fails when decision words appear with no YES/NO labels.
The flowchart type is aimed at decision logic, branching user flows, onboarding routing and triage trees, which matches Product Owner input material rather than architecture vocabulary.
sk-design-diagram supports only html-svg and ascii-markdown and its skip list names canvas artifacts, so FigJam must port the rules rather than reuse the renderer.
